raw_record.question_text: Three point charges of \(+Q\), \(+2Q\), and \(-Q\) are each located a distance \(r\) away from the origin, as shown above. What is the magnitude of the electric field at the origin due to these charges?

method.method_draft: Use Cartesian vector components. First read the diagram: the +Q charge is at (-r, 0), the +2Q charge is at (+r, 0), and the -Q charge is at (0, +r), with the origin O at the axes intersection. From the text, all charges are distance r from the origin and the task asks for the electric-field magnitude at O. Let E0 = kQ/r^2. At O, the field from +Q at the left points in the +x direction with magnitude E0; the field from +2Q at the right points in the -x direction with magnitude 2E0; the field from -Q above points toward the negative charge, i.e. in the +y direction, with magnitude E0. Add components: Ex = E0 - 2E0 = -E0 and Ey = E0. Then take the magnitude sqrt(Ex^2 + Ey^2) = sqrt(2)E0 = sqrt(2)kQ/r^2.

method.method_draft: Use cancellation by decomposing the +2Q charge. Read the diagram as showing +Q at (-r,0), +2Q at (+r,0), and -Q at (0,+r), all one distance r from O. Treat the +2Q charge on the right as two identical +Q charges located together at (+r,0). One of those right-side +Q contributions produces a field of magnitude kQ/r^2 toward -x at the origin, which exactly cancels the field of magnitude kQ/r^2 toward +x from the left-side +Q charge. The remaining right-side +Q contribution gives a field of magnitude kQ/r^2 toward -x. The top -Q charge gives a field of magnitude kQ/r^2 toward +y. These two remaining equal-magnitude perpendicular fields combine to give sqrt((kQ/r^2)^2 + (kQ/r^2)^2) = sqrt(2)kQ/r^2.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：两张附图显示同一电荷布局：坐标原点 O 在水平轴和竖直轴交点处；+Q 位于左侧 (-r,0)；+2Q 位于右侧 (+r,0)；-Q 位于上方 (0,+r)。三个电荷到原点的距离都为 r。推理：按照题设方法，把右侧的 +2Q 看成两个重合的 +Q。左侧 (-r,0) 的 +Q 在原点产生大小 kQ/r²、方向沿 +x 的电场；右侧 (+r,0) 的其中一个 +Q 在原点产生大小 kQ/r²、方向沿 -x 的电场，这两者相互抵消。右侧剩余的一个 +Q 仍在原点产生大小 kQ/r²、方向沿 -x 的电场。上方 (0,+r) 的 -Q 在原点产生大小 kQ/r²、方向朝向负电荷，即沿 +y。于是剩下两个互相垂直且等大的电场分量，合场强大小为 sqrt((kQ/r²)^2 + (kQ/r²)^2) = √2 kQ/r²。
